1932829430692618636 [2025-06-11] @FU_joehudson 💜 204 🔁 10
A major pitfall I see that drives conflict in relationships is the belief that:

"If I can shape their world, I won’t have to feel my own helplessness."

For example, I met a man once who was constantly trying to make his wife feel happy...

↓
↓
1932829442516398565 [2025-06-11] @FU_joehudson 💜 22 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
Meanwhile, his wife was getting more and more resentful of him. Their relationship was going in a horrible direction.

Baffled, the man came to me and asked me what he was doing wrong.

As we peeled back the layers, we began to see the real dynamic.
↓
1932829454537273490 [2025-06-11] @FU_joehudson 💜 29
The subtle message he was sending her by constantly trying to keep her happy was:

I need to make you happy because I don’t trust you to handle your own life.
↓
1932829466386182265 [2025-06-11] @FU_joehudson 💜 23
She was being treated like a child, not a partner.

And the predictable result was that of anger—sometimes a tight-lipped sigh, sometimes a full-blown fight.
↓
1932829478176358566 [2025-06-11] @FU_joehudson 💜 28
Together, we tried something new: Instead of trying to fix her all the time, he decided to just be there with her.

Rather than saying: “This is what I would do,” he said “What do you want to do about that?” or “How do you want to handle that?”
↓
1932829489953923493 [2025-06-11] @FU_joehudson 💜 24 🔁 1
As he did this, he noticed the twitch of panic when he couldn’t “make it better.”

He realized that, one layer deeper, he had been trying to have power over her happiness all because he didn’t want to feel his own helplessness.
↓
1932829501765136400 [2025-06-11] @FU_joehudson 💜 68 🔁 3
Once he saw this, he decided to feel his own helplessness. He sat with the vulnerability instead of covering it with advice.

And once he welcomed his helplessness, he no longer needed to have power over her. He could be okay no matter how she felt.
↓
1932829513639178434 [2025-06-11] @FU_joehudson 💜 23
From then on, when she came to him, he listened and empathized. He waited for her to ask for help before offering it.
↓
1932829525559423167 [2025-06-11] @FU_joehudson 💜 26
Within weeks the atmosphere shifted.  The resentment melted because the power imbalance that fueled it was gone.

===
